title: Looking for nerve problems caused by chemotherapy: determining the effectiveness of an early identification screening programme
official: Screening for chemotherapy induced peripheral neuropathy: determining the effectiveness of an early identification screening programme
summary:
Background and study aims 
Children receiving chemotherapy may develop chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) during their treatment. CIPN is defined as any injury, inflammation or degeneration of peripheral nerves due to chemotherapy. Peripheral nerves are those nerves outside the brain and spinal cord, e.g., those in the arms and legs. Signs and symptoms of CIPN include pain, muscle weakness, sensory problems (e.g., pins and needles) and autonomic involvement (e.g. constipation). Progressive weakness and pain can lead to walking and balance problems.
There are currently no guidelines or evidence on how best to identify CIPN, and it is unknown if early therapy intervention can help longer-term outcomes.

This study aims to find out how feasible it is to carry out a study that tests the impact of a screening programme for CIPN on children’s long-term physical outcomes.

Who can participate? 
Newly diagnosed children aged 4-<18 years who are at high risk of CIPN.

What does the study involve? 
The researchers want to find out whether spotting nerve problems early through screening can help improve outcomes for children, such as reducing pain or helping them walk more easily. Before doing a large study, they first need to check that all parts of the research are practical and acceptable to both children and their parents. To do this, they will run a small‑scale version of the study to see what works well and what may need to be changed. This study will compare the usual care children receive with a screening programme designed to detect chemotherapy‑related nerve problems at an earlier stage.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating? 
Benefits and risks not provided at time of registration

Where is the study run from?  
Alder Hey Childrens NHS Foundation Trust, UK.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for? 
August 2023 to June 2026.

Who is funding the study? 
1. Charitable Funding at Alder Hey Children’s NHS Foundation Trust, UK.
2. Isle of Man Anti-Cancer Association, Isle of Man.

Who is the main contact?
Dr Helen Hartley, helen.hartley@alderhey.nhs.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Newly diagnosed children, 4-<18 years at high risk of CIPN (this will encompass the following diagnoses: children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia (ALL), Wilms Tumour, Rhabdomyosarcoma, Low grade brain tumour on LGG 2 Protocol). 
These children are classed as high risk of CIPN as their treatment protocol includes weekly vincristine during their treatment schedule. High incidence of CIPN in these patient groups has been reported in the literature.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Medically unstable or presence of co-morbidities affecting safety of screening/outcome measure assessments, or those with relapsed disease.
2. Under the age of 4 years due to inability to complete the chosen outcome measures
